hero_kpi_rationale: The volume of ExtraCash is a key indicator of the company's activity and its success in providing low-cost liquidity to consumers. With $22 billion provided to over 14 million members, this KPI reflects traction in the flagship product and the platform's ability to serve consumers living paycheck to paycheck.

kpis.explanation: Number of members who have used at least one product from the company.
kpis.description: The number of active members who have used at least one product is an indicator of platform traction and adoption.
kpis.signal: Growth in number of active members

kpis.name: Volume of ExtraCash provided
kpis.explanation: Volume of ExtraCash provided to members since inception.
kpis.description: The volume of ExtraCash is an indicator of the company's activity and the liquidity provided to consumers.

kpis.name: Average revenue per user
kpis.explanation: Average revenue generated per user, primarily through ExtraCash and adoption of Dave Checking.
kpis.description: ARPU is an indicator of user profitability and engagement. Dave Checking debit card holders generate 1.7x higher monthly ARPU than non-card users.
kpis.signal: ARPU expansion via ExtraCash volume and Dave Checking adoption

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.description: Gross margin is an indicator of the company's profitability. High interest rates impact financing costs of ExtraCash receivables and reduce gross margins.

kpis.name: Research and development investments
kpis.explanation: Investments in research and development, including CashAI credit technology.
kpis.description: R&D investments, particularly in CashAI v5.5, are an indicator of technological innovation. CashAI benefits from over 180 million ExtraCash originations to refine real-time credit decisioning models.
kpis.signal: Innovation via CashAI and improvement in credit models

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.description: Capital expenditures support platform growth, reliability, and security, including technology infrastructure and SaaS costs.

kpis.name: Volume of ExtraCash provided
kpis.explanation: Volume of ExtraCash provided to members since inception.
kpis.description: The $22 billion ExtraCash volume provided to over 14 million members demonstrates traction in the flagship product and the platform's impact on access to affordable credit.

risks.title: Increasing credit loss provisions
risks.score_rationale: Credit loss provisions increased to $37.6 million in 2025 from $22.7 million in 2024 (65.6% increase). This risk reflects growth in ExtraCash volume and expansion of the member base. While the increase is expected, it is significant and reflects the platform's growing credit exposure. Severe economic conditions could materially increase defaults.

risks.title: Dependence on processing fee revenue
risks.score_rationale: Processing fee revenue constitutes the majority of service revenue. The 5% minimum $5 fee structure for overdraft services (implemented in February 2025) improves monetization but creates dependence on continued approval and usage of ExtraCash. Sensitivity to regulatory changes or consumer preferences remains high.

risks.title: High customer acquisition and marketing costs
risks.score_rationale: Customer acquisition cost remained around $19 in 2025. Advertising and activation expenses support member acquisition and product growth. Although payback periods have improved to under four months (the fastest on record), marketing spend must remain high to sustain growth.

risks.title: Product concentration risk
risks.score_rationale: ExtraCash remains the primary driver of engagement and revenue. While Dave Checking is growing (debit card spend reached $534 million in Q4 2025, up 17% year-over-year, with 1.7x higher ARPU than non-users), the platform remains dependent on a single credit product for a significant portion of revenue and engagement.

risks.title: Interest rate sensitivity and funding risk
risks.score_rationale: ExtraCash receivables depend on financing through a variable-rate debt facility, exposing the platform to interest rate risk. Higher rates increase financing costs, reducing ExtraCash unit economics. The program agreement with Coastal (March 2025) is expected to reduce financing obligations, but creates indirect exposure to variable rates maintained by Coastal.

risks.title: Banking transition risk with Coastal
risks.score_rationale: The program agreement with Coastal (March 2025) for deposit and network access services is a major change. All new members are onboarded via Coastal, and the transition of existing members is expected to be largely completed by end of 2026. The success of this transition directly affects the reduction of financing costs and the off-balance sheet structure of ExtraCash receivables.

risks.title: Macroeconomic conditions risk
risks.score_rationale: Economic conditions, particularly unemployment and consumer spending, materially influence members' repayment capacity. Reports indicate that 67% of U.S. consumers live paycheck to paycheck (December 2025), but a severe economic downturn could materially increase defaults and charge-offs despite refinements in CashAI models.

risks.title: Increasing competition
risks.score_rationale: Dave competes with traditional banks, neobanks (Chime, Varo), short-term credit providers (Earnin, MoneyLion, Brigit), and broader fintech platforms (Affirm, Cash App, Venmo). Many competitors have superior financial resources, longer operating histories, and larger customer bases. Dave differentiates through its value proposition (interest-free credit up to $500), CashAI technology, and customer satisfaction.

risks.title: Rising technology and infrastructure costs
risks.score_rationale: Technology and infrastructure costs are increasing to support reliability, security, and continuous innovation (CashAI v5.5, real-time cash flow underwriting). While the platform is technically efficient, reliance on SaaS solutions and security investments represent a growing recurring cost.

risks.title: Dependence on banking partners
risks.score_rationale: Dave relies on banking partners for deposit services, network access, and financing. The agreement with Coastal is critical to reducing financing costs, but creates dependence on a third party for core banking services. Any dispute or termination with a key banking partner could disrupt operations.

ai_positioning.summary: Dave actively uses artificial intelligence across its CashAI platform, a proprietary credit underwriting engine, to optimize real-time credit decisions and improve member outcomes.
evidence: CashAI v5.5 deployed in September 2025 with a feature set nearly doubled compared to prior versions
CashAI has leveraged insights from over 180 million ExtraCash originations to create a structural advantage in real-time credit decisioning
Early results show improved risk scoring, higher average approval amounts, and lower delinquency rates
Fast feedback loops (average ExtraCash duration of approximately 11 days) enable iterative model refinement
Real-time cash flow underwriting detects changes in income, expenses, and employment for continuous risk assessment
